:::{#exm-sigma-finite}
#### Finite and $\sigma$-finite measures

- Every finite measure is $\sigma$-finite:
  take $A_1 = S$ and

  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  A_2 &= A_3 \\
  &= \cdots \\
  &= \emptyset,
  \end{aligned}
  $$

  with $\measure(A_1) = \measure(S) < \infty$ and $\measure(\emptyset) = 0$.
- The counting measure on the die rolls $D$ is finite, with $\measure(D) = 6$.
- The counting measure on $\set{0, 1, 2, \ldots}$ is not finite,
  but it is $\sigma$-finite:
  it is the union of the sets $A_i = \set{0, 1, \ldots, i}$,
  each with $\measure(A_i) = i + 1 < \infty$.
- Lebesgue measure on $\reals$ is not finite,
  since $\lebesgue(\reals) = \infty$,
  but it is $\sigma$-finite:
  $\reals$ is the union of the intervals $A_i = [-i, i]$,
  each with $\lebesgue(A_i) = 2i < \infty$.

:::
